name: Authoritarian Conservatism
summary: Authoritarian conservatism defends order, hierarchy, tradition and religion, and accepts strong, often unelected central authority and forcible suppression of revolutionaries to keep them. It is nationalist and anti-communist but traditionalist rather than revolutionary, which separates it from fascism. Its economics vary from corporatism to laissez-faire.
scope: The mainstream interwar and Cold War right-wing authoritarian regimes and thinkers: Maistre's ultra-royalist and ultramontane thought, Schmitt's decisionism, and regimes such as Salazar's Estado Novo, Franco, Pétain, Metaxas, Pinochet and Park Chung Hee. Burke is used as the root of the wider conservative tradition, not as an authoritarian. Excludes fascism and modern liberal or libertarian conservatism.

sources.title: Conservatism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: National conservatism, family, church-state cooperation, welfare and the authoritarian variant.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Economic stance varies by regime (Salazar's limited welfare, Pinochet's market reforms); no doctrinal commitment to state-guaranteed health care, though paternalist regimes provided insurance schemes.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Regimes set wages by decree or left them to markets; substantial worker-favouring increases are not a defining aim and were often subordinated to order and discipline.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The documented record is split between corporatist state direction (Portugal) and laissez-faire (Pinochet's Chicago Boys), so adherents genuinely differ.

public-ownership.rationale: Corporatist regimes preferred private property under state supervision; wholesale public ownership of utilities is not a core aim, though strategic state control occurred.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Hierarchy and property are defended; redistributive taxation of elites runs against the order-preserving instinct, though noblesse oblige tempers this.

unions-good.rationale: Free unions were replaced by state-run syndicates in Estado Novo; independent labour organisation is seen as a source of class conflict and disorder.

property-fundamental.rationale: Burke tied liberty to property and conservatives name private property as a source of stability, but authoritarian regimes override it when the state judges it necessary.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Corporatist states tightly regulated business through state-recognised bodies, while market-oriented authoritarian regimes deregulated; no common line.

cut-welfare.rationale: Paternalist conservatism supports a limited safety net (Bismarck, Salazar's 1933 system), while market-leaning variants cut benefits; adherents split.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective worker ownership belongs to the socialist revolution these regimes were built to suppress; corporatism instead keeps owners and workers as partners under state arbitration.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Regimes relied on secret police such as the PIDE and treated surveillance of subversives as a normal tool of order.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Order, tradition and moral discipline favour prohibition; permissiveness is regarded as decadent.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Speech laws are not a hate-speech question for these regimes: they censor dissent and radicalism broadly but have no commitment to protecting minorities as such.

strong-leader.rationale: Schmitt's decisionist sovereign and the dictatorial presidency are central, and Fawcett describes the ideology as fear of democracy taken to extremes.

state-harmful.rationale: The ideology is built on strong centralised authority and the state as guarantor of order, the opposite of anarchism.

limit-guns.rationale: Regimes monopolised arms for state forces and disarmed opponents, but there is no doctrine on civilian gun ownership; Western variants support gun rights.

empower-police-military.rationale: Forcible suppression of radical enemies by police and army is a defining feature in the Wikipedia account.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Catholic family-centred morality of the Estado Novo ("God, Fatherland and Family") treats sex work as a moral offence.

decide-locally.rationale: Strong centralised authority is the ideological norm, though traditional local bodies and families get some organic role.

rehabilitation.rationale: Maistre's praise of the executioner and the emphasis on punishment and deterrence rank retribution above reform.

traditional-family.rationale: "God, Fatherland and Family" was the Estado Novo motto and Salazar opposed what weakened the family.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Defence of tradition and religion makes redefining marriage firmly opposed; inferred from traditional-religious basis.

abortion-legal.rationale: Catholic social doctrine and traditional religion underlie the regime philosophy, and permissive abortion contradicts it.

more-religion-public.rationale: The ideology is grounded in traditional religion, in contrast with fascism's vitalism or secularism.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Hierarchy and gradualism oppose activist redress; inferred, since regimes seldom framed the question this way.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Traditional religion and family doctrine hold that sex roles are given by nature and God; inferred from regime family ideology.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Authoritarian conservatism combines devotion to religion, tradition and culture with strong nationalism.

gradual-change.rationale: Conservatives prize established institutions and gradualism, yet authoritarian conservatives use force and emergency rule to halt change, and reactionaries seek to restore the past.

reduce-immigration.rationale: National conservatism favours limited immigration, but historic regimes seldom treated it centrally; inferred from nationalism.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Sovereignty and nationalism lead adherents to resist supranational authority; Portugal joined the UN and NATO only pragmatically.

free-trade.rationale: The Estado Novo ran a protectionist, state-approved economy and a closed imperial escudo area, though Pinochet's Chile liberalised.

nation-first.rationale: Nationalism is shared with fascism and defines the ideology's outward stance.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Sovereignty and non-interference are favoured; inferred from nationalism and Estado Novo neutrality.

open-borders.rationale: National identity and sovereignty are central, so removing borders is rejected.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmental degrowth is not part of the doctrine and regimes pursued development; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from scepticism of rationalist, state-driven transformation by abstract schemes, tempered by statism.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Traditionalism distrusts progress as a creed, yet authoritarian modernisers (Park Chung Hee) pursued industrialisation; split.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Never addressed; state-directed energy and strength favour it as an inference.

revolution-justified.rationale: Opposition to revolutionary upheaval is the defining stance, and Maistre read the Revolution as divine punishment.

experts-over-public.rationale: Hierarchy and fear of democratic participation favour elite or technocratic rule over the mass public.

central-planning.rationale: Regimes favoured state-guided or corporatist economies but not full planning that abolishes private ownership.

socialized-markets.rationale: Socialist ownership schemes are rejected as part of the leftist threat.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed by the ideology; no basis for a stance.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Burke defended hereditary property and inheritance as underpinning the social order.

basic-income.rationale: Paternalist conservatism favours duty and discipline over unconditional state payments; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The Estado Novo was protectionist and used tariffs and a captive imperial market.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The Portuguese state approved major investments and corporatist states steered the economy.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Catholic social doctrine behind the Estado Novo favoured broad property ownership and a rural smallholder ideal; inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Rooted in the opposition to communism and radical enemies.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A strong state keeps its monetary institutions; abolition is a radical, anti-statist idea.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Portugal's corporatism was authoritarian Catholic and organised interest groups into state-recognised corporations; Pinochet-style variants differed.

one-party-rule.rationale: Some regimes banned other parties (Carol II), but Salazar rejected the party-state and kept a passive National Union; adherents split.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Maistre saw monarchy as divinely sanctioned and the only stable form, though many authoritarian conservatives ran republics or military regimes.

democracy-best.rationale: Fawcett describes democratic participation as the ideology's enemy and fear of democracy as its hallmark.

direct-votes.rationale: Mass participation is distrusted and regimes limited representation.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils as the basis of power are a communist or radical idea that these movements suppressed.

right-to-secede.rationale: Estado Novo held its empire as extensions of Portugal; unity of the state is paramount.

natural-rulers.rationale: Social stratification and rule by a legitimate elite follow from the hierarchical view of Maistre and Burke.

political-violence-never.rationale: Forcible suppression of enemies and violence by the state are accepted; some also treat revolution as pernicious.

war-builds-character.rationale: Nationalist and martial rhetoric appear in some regimes, while others like Portugal stayed neutral in WWII; split.

separate-church-state.rationale: Continental conservatives favour state cooperation with the Church, and Maistre founded legitimacy on religion.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Maistre wanted authority derived from religion, and the Estado Novo drew on papal encyclicals rather than scripture directly; adherents differ on scripture as law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state monopoly on force and justice is central to the order-focused doctrine.

military-superiority.rationale: Strong nationalism and army-backed rule favour a powerful military, though Portugal was neutral in WWII.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Nationalism is shared with fascism, but traditionalist regimes were generally religion- or empire-centred (pluricontinental Portugal) rather than ethnic.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Class conflict as the engine of history is the Marxist view the regimes fought; they preached class cooperation.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Burke rooted the social order in inequality and conservatives reject equality as an abstract value.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Estado Novo treated colonies as part of Portugal; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Regimes defended empire and resisted decolonisation, justified by lusotropicalism.

civilizational-union.rationale: Some regimes pursued pan-religious ideas but nationalism usually dominated; split and unaddressed.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Conservatives see human nature as selfish and fallible and stress duty and community over self-interest as a moral guide.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Maistre and Burke defended traditional authority and inherited liberties rather than universal rights, and corporatist doctrine stresses duty.

limit-population.rationale: Catholic and pronatalist family doctrine opposes coercive population limits; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Some conservatives criticised industrialisation but regimes pursued development.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Conservatives prefer stability to improvement and reject disruption of existing institutions.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Authority is personal and traditional rather than algorithmic; anachronistic and inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A surveillance-dependent state cannot accept citizens beyond its reach.

restore-past-order.rationale: The reactionary strand puts restoration first, though mainstream conservatives want gradual change; leaning agree.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Conservatives distrust ideology, as Oakeshott's pragmatism shows, but authoritarian regimes rest on explicit doctrines; split.

direct-action.rationale: Revolutionary or street-level challenges to the order are what the ideology suppresses.

means-match-ends.rationale: Regimes openly used coercion for order and did not require methods to prefigure ends; inferred.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Hierarchy and stratified roles are defended.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Communist principle opposed by the doctrine.

production-for-use.rationale: A socialist aim at odds with private property under corporatism.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Corporatism preached class collaboration rather than exploitation theory.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The ideology exists to suppress communists and radicals.

collective-farming.rationale: Regimes favoured smallholders and private landowners.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis rejected by these anti-communist regimes.

taxation-theft.rationale: Strong-state conservatives accept taxation as a state power.

harm-principle.rationale: Moral order, religion and tradition justify restrictions beyond harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Conservatives rejected universal natural rights, valuing inherited liberties and communal bodies like family and corporation.

conscription.rationale: A strong military state and nationalism accept compulsory service.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Libertarian idea; regimes restricted both voice and often exit, and it clashes with duties to the nation.

state-as-business.rationale: Authority is rooted in tradition and duty, not consumer exit; Pinochet-style technocrats partly differ.

positive-liberty.rationale: Oakeshott holds there is no freedom without authority, but material-means welfare claims are not core.

media-academia-power.rationale: Critics such as John Dean link modern social conservatism to this view; Cold War regimes feared intellectual subversion, but evidence is mixed.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Some regimes held racial ideas, but the traditionalist religious stream mostly rejects biological race doctrine as fascist; split.

organic-representation.rationale: Estado Novo corporatism replaced parties with state-recognised corporations and family and local bodies.

total-state.rationale: Fawcett says authoritarian regimes permit independent economic and social bodies, unlike totalitarian fascism, though the state is strong.

national-rebirth.rationale: Rebirth is palingenetic fascist language; authoritarian conservatives are traditionalist rather than revolutionary.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Estado Novo sought to keep its empire, not expand; mostly defensive, though some regimes differed.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal personal oaths are not part of modern regimes.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is not advocated by modern authoritarian conservatives, though agrarian hierarchy is accepted; inferred.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Conservatives rely on objective, inherited truth and religion; this is a postmodern critical claim.

universal-morality.rationale: Maistre grounded authority in divinely sanctioned truth, but he rejected reason as the means of knowing it; leaning agree with the "by reason" wording as the weak point.

single-common-good.rationale: Corporatism sought national harmony in one common good under authority rather than competing group interests.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Hierarchy and corporatist class collaboration reject democratic control of firms.

school-vouchers.rationale: Church-run schooling interest conflicts with state control of education; split.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Salazar was known for balanced budgets; inferred, and not universal.

economic-freedom.rationale: Pinochet's regime held economic freedom before political, while others disagree; split.

rule-by-example.rationale: Maistre and traditional elites hold moral authority matters, yet regimes also rely heavily on laws and punishment; split.

national-self-determination.rationale: Nationalism supports own nation's self-rule, but empires (Portugal) denied it to colonies.

force-without-un.rationale: Sovereignty-minded nationalism accepts unilateral force; inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Maistre blamed rationalism and Bacon; faith and tradition ground legitimacy.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: National conservatism limits benefits to the national community; inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Paternalist discipline favours conditional welfare; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Corporatism organises employers and workers as partners under the state.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Burke's inherited institutions and tradition are valued.

dominated-front.rationale: Not an issue the doctrine addresses; Portugal sided with the West.

workers-nation.rationale: Corporatist national syndicates tied workers to the nation, opposing internationalism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: "God, Fatherland and Family" implies distinct roles, though Estado Novo allowed some women's suffrage in 1933.

ban-interest.rationale: Catholic social doctrine criticised usury historically, but regimes allowed banking; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Race laws belong to fascist and some colonial regimes; traditionalist Catholic regimes mostly did not make this central.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist theory rejected by these regimes.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: National culture preservation implies assimilation; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: A modern conspiracy claim, not part of the classical doctrine; contested among adherents.

proportional-representation.rationale: Parliamentary party competition is distrusted; the Estado Novo's assembly was limited to National Union members.

national-mission.rationale: Portugal's "civilising" pluricontinental claim existed, but exporting a government form is not typical of these regimes.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Family and gender hierarchy is regarded as natural order, not an injustice.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Regimes claim to be above corrupt parties, while critics note elite privilege; split.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The PIDE persecuted dissenters and regimes shielded security forces from accountability.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Strong centralised authority with wide moral and social roles is the aim.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not a core traditionalist position; regimes like Portugal promoted lusotropical mixing ideology.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Burke rooted the social order in inequality, yet Christian doctrine teaches equal souls; equality before the law is not an aim.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist doctrinal question; adherents reject socialism entirely.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Regimes regarded colonial settlement as legitimate national extension.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic regimes favoured religious family law, but unity of state favours uniformity.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Established religion supporters may restrict proselytism, but this is not defined in the doctrine.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A Hindu-specific question the doctrine never addressed.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The Church shaped Estado Novo education and religion was central to the regime.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist argument not used by this ideology.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Fawcett's account stresses fear of democracy; legitimacy comes from tradition, religion or the sovereign rather than popular consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Salazar's protectionist, balanced-budget economy favoured export-minded and saving policies; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Some regimes expelled enemies, but not defining; unsupported.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The ideology accepts forcible suppression by the state.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Conservatives prize stability and order over struggle as the engine of progress; the social Darwinian view belongs more to fascism.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Regimes banned communist and radical parties and suppressed enemies by force.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican concept; conservatives accept authority and defend traditional liberties rather than non-domination.

separated-powers.rationale: Schmitt criticised liberal separation of powers and favoured concentrated executive power.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist concept opposed by these regimes.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Paternalist and Christian duty to the poor exists (Disraeli, noblesse oblige), but not as a first priority of laws; split.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Free unions were replaced by state-controlled syndicates and disorder is suppressed.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: National conservatism's cultural cohesion emphasis suggests agreement, but traditionalist regimes seldom put it centrally; inferred.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Rule by qualified authority and hierarchy rejects lot selection.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Schmitt's sovereign decides on the exception and may act outside the rule of law.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: State-directed economies fixed prices in scarcity, but liberalising variants disagreed; split.

party-controls-media.rationale: Censorship was routine but Salazar rejected a party-state; control by state rather than party.

party-commands-army.rationale: Authoritarian conservatives rely on the army and state, not a party army, and distrust party-state fascism.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: National conservatism favours restricted naturalisation; inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Hierarchy and distinguished elites favour no such leveling.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party discipline is not defining; many regimes restrict parties instead.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: National conservatives are usually Eurosceptics and defend sovereignty.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Schmitt favoured a strong president who decides in emergencies, and regimes concentrate command in the head of state.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Maistre's ultramontane, papal-hierarchical Catholicism favours bishops and the Pope's authority.

clerical-rule.rationale: Estado Novo and others kept the Church influential but under secular rulers; theocracy is not typical.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism contradicts nationalism and order.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Moral order and religion support cultural censorship, as practised by Estado Novo.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Dictatorial leaders like Salazar held power indefinitely; strong leader rule implies no limit.

recall-officials.rationale: Mass-participatory removal of officials is democratic and distrusted.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Portugal was a NATO founder; alliances were used pragmatically.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Radical economic measure opposed to property rights.

people-in-arms.rationale: These regimes rely on professional armies and distrust an armed populace.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Estado Novo's rural, traditional ideal; inferred, as not universally stated.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Mixed: anti-intellectualism exists in reactionary strands, but regimes also prize elites.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Hierarchy and cultural pride, with Maistre judging Revolutionary reason inferior, are against equal valuing of civilisations.

death-penalty.rationale: Maistre praised the executioner as pillar of order, and state execution of grave crimes is accepted.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Catholic moral education opposes progressive sex and gender curricula; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Traditional religion favours religion in schools, but Catholic regimes did not usually push creationism; split.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Moral order and religion support it; the Estado Novo censored material for virtue.

minority-language-support.rationale: Centralised national culture is favoured; minority claims seen as divisive.

religious-exemptions.rationale: A unified order and established religion favour uniform law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Custom and conformity are valued, in contrast to Mill's call for eccentricity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Respect for obligations and property; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Regimes resisted decolonisation and are indifferent to this thesis; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Maistre held constitutions are not made by human reason or assemblies but grow under divine guidance.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Park Chung Hee's and Pinochet's regimes justified authoritarian rule by development.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Strong sovereign nationalism favours independence in defense; inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Estado Novo had an indirectly elected or rigged president; authoritarian presidents sometimes got plebiscites (Schmitt), split.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Portugal refused to cede territory in colonial war; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Catholic social doctrine behind corporatism subordinates property to social purposes.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist debate not addressed; adherents simply oppose the USSR.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed; scepticism of regulatory expansion inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Portugal was a NATO founder and these regimes aligned with anti-communist alliances.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Estado Novo and Maistre's ultramontanism cooperate with the Church and defend its authority.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Schmitt's president as guardian above parties; authoritarian regimes present the ruler as above partisanship.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The Estado Novo fought the Colonial War to keep territories as extensions of Portugal.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Maistre held monarchy divinely sanctioned, but sacred divine descent is specific to Japanese-type ideology; most adherents do not claim it.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The doctrine has no tax-structure position, and Pinochet-style market reformers and paternalist corporatists would differ, so it is a genuine split.

character-from-environment.rationale: Conservatives see human nature as weak and fixed and reject Rousseau's optimism, so innate nature matters.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy never featured in the sources; traditionalist and nationalist outlooks give no clear lean, so neutral.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Burke admired the British mix, while authoritarian conservatives concentrate power; split.

leader-cult.rationale: Personal rule glorification varies: Salazar avoided it while some regimes embraced it.

equal-parenting.rationale: Traditional family roles favour mothers; inferred.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist question the doctrine rejects.

land-redistribution.rationale: Property and hereditary estates are defended, and redistribution is a leftist measure.

refugee-return.rationale: No source treats refugee return, and the answer would depend on the national interest in each case, so neutral.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Nationalism sometimes supports it (Hungary, Germany) but not defined.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Catholic regimes did not usually punish apostasy by law in the 20th century; inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: A specific Islamic law; Catholic traditionalism supports modesty but not legal coverings, though Iran's Principlists differ.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Nationalist regimes sometimes sought kin unity but traditionalists mostly defended existing states; the sources are silent, so neutral.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority strategy for emigration versus local rights is not discussed in the sources and is not an issue the ideology defines.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Maistre saw history as divinely guided and driven by religion and ideas; Marxist materialism is rejected.

ban-cartels.rationale: Corporatist structures organised producers collectively; inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; split between market and statist variants.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Majority rule is distrusted, while the executive is also placed above courts in an emergency; the statement favours liberal democracy's majority, which adherents reject.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas conflict with traditional roles.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Estado Novo built an economically integrated empire (the escudo area), a protectionist bloc.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding international standards touch sovereignty, which these adherents oppose, but protectionists might welcome them; the sources are silent.

moral-incentives.rationale: Moral duty is emphasised, but Marxist moral incentives schemes are not.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Burke defended hereditary succession and rank as the spirit of the constitution.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Nationalism and culture preservation favour a nation-centred history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Estado Novo justified empire by lusotropicalism, ruling for the colonies' improvement.

patriotic-education.rationale: Mocidade Portuguesa and "God, Fatherland and Family" instilled national loyalty.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed by historical doctrine; modern adherents likely agree but cases vary.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from property orientation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Anti-Marxist stance rejects collapse theory; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Estado Novo's lusotropicalism and continuing influence in former territories; inferred for others.

delink-world-market.rationale: A leftist dependency idea; economic nationalism exists but not delinking.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Moral order and state regulation of society override pure private freedom, though property is valued.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Conservatives reject abstract universal rights, as the Declaration of 1789 was rejected.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Regimes defended colonial settlements and empire.

elective-rulers.rationale: Maistre favoured hereditary monarchy over election, though other regimes used elections as formalities.

minority-veto.rationale: Order and authority reject a veto power for dissenters.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Maistre held government legitimacy rests on religious grounds that subjects may not question; Burke permitted resistance only in extremes.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The 1933 Constitution created an anti-parliamentary system.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; conventional tradition accepts use of animals with humane restraint; inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Paternalist conservatism holds the wealthy owe obligations to those below, as in Disraeli's One Nation.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Duty to community and nation requires engagement in the order.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A critical theory claim opposed by conservatives, though they also feared popular culture's moral effect.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian thesis; adherents do not use it.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: A dependency theory rejected by anti-leftist ideology.

native-born-offices.rationale: National conservatism restricts offices to the national community; inferred.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Nationalism and thrifty economy favour self-reliance; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Regimes held settlers' or colonial rule legitimate; hierarchy rejects this.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Authoritarian conservatives cooperated with fascists in places and clash with the left's founding myths, though they also opposed fascists in Austria and Portugal.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The ideology is anti-communist and distinguishes itself from fascism, but condemns both as radical revolutionary movements.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American historiographic issue not addressed by the ideology.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Respect for inheritance and tradition favours preservation.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; traditional roles imply little interest in gender-neutral programmes, though modern conservatives may agree.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents' traditional family views point both ways, so neutral.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Nationalist traditionalism holds institutions must fit national tradition, and Maistre scorned imported abstract constitutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Armies as guardians of order are characteristic: Park, Pinochet, Chiang, Lon Nol.

paid-care-work.rationale: Traditional family roles treat care as family duty, not paid labour.

filial-duty.rationale: Family-centred order and hierarchy; Confucian and Catholic variants stress it.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not addressed; hierarchy favours merit, but patronage also used.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Catholic family doctrine opposed easy divorce.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Protectionist, nationalist economy of the Estado Novo; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Burke tied liberties to landed hereditary property.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pinochet privatised pensions while corporatist regimes used state insurance; adherents split.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Schmitt favoured executive action beyond parliament; regimes weakened budget control; some formal approval retained.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics belongs to fascist and racial regimes; Catholic traditionalism condemns coercive eugenics, though it is inferred, not documented here.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Schmitt held the sovereign decides on the exception and may act beyond the rule of law, though traditionalists like Maistre bound rulers by divine law.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from nationalism and the drive for a unified, hierarchical national order; the sources do not discuss language policy.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from nationalism and the protectionist, corporatist character of regimes like the Estado Novo.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from its acceptance of natural hierarchy and rejection of egalitarianism.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from the austerity and anti-materialism of regimes such as Salazar's and its religious traditionalism.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from its militant anti-communism; Cold War right-wing regimes backed forces against communist governments.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Nationalist emphasis on sovereignty cuts against forcible intervention, though anti-communist solidarity could favour it; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Varies by regime; corporatist ones control business while others support private elites; no shared line.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Authoritarian regimes of this tradition restricted foreign-backed organisations and media as subversive; inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Estado Novo, Franco and Vichy promoted large families and the traditional family as national duty.

residents-only-property.rationale: No documented line; property protection by landowning elites suggests mixed views.

job-guarantee.rationale: Corporatist regimes organised labour under state control but did not guarantee jobs; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: These regimes were suspicious of liberal democracy and its export; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Maistre and Schmitt ground legitimacy in authority and obedience, so duty to obey law and the sovereign is central.

non-intervention.rationale: Sovereignty and non-interference are valued, though anti-communist interventions were accepted; inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Corporatist unions were organised by state vertical sectors; independent industrial unions were suppressed; inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Some regimes (Vichy, Franco) pushed conspiracy claims about Jews or Freemasons while others did not; split.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage and religion-based family are central to the tradition, so abolishing legal marriage is firmly rejected.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Secrecy and state authority are favoured; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Rural traditionalism appeals, but no stated stance on localised production.

informal-organisation.rationale: Hierarchical, permanent institutions are central, and informal anti-authority groups are alien and suppressed.

national-law-over-international.rationale: National sovereignty over international bodies fits the tradition; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Catholic and religious foundations of the nation are central to Maistre, Salazar and Franco.

missingStatements.text: Armies and police should be used to crush radical movements that threaten the established order.
missingStatements.rationale: Forcible suppression of communists, Nazis and anarchists is the definitional practice of the ideology.

missingStatements.text: Political authority should be based on religious grounds that subjects may not question.
missingStatements.rationale: Maistre held government legitimacy must rest on unquestionable religious foundations.

notes: Economic answers are low-confidence because adherents split between corporatists (Salazar) and market liberalisers (Pinochet). Burke is cited for conservative roots only, and only the opening of Reflections was read.
